facts.fact: Adwave states that a $25 CPM is the middle of CTV's typical $15-35 CPM range, and at that CPM $1,000 buys 40,000 impressions.
facts.quote: At a $25 CPM (the middle of CTV's typical $15-35 range, explained in our [CPM guide]

facts.fact: Adwave says that recognition research has shown meaningful recall starts around the third exposure to an ad, though the page does not name the study.
facts.quote: recognition research has shown for decades that meaningful recall starts around the third exposure

facts.fact: Adwave recommends planning for at least 3-4 exposures per household per month as a frequency floor.
facts.quote: plan for at least 3-4 exposures per household per month

facts.fact: Adwave treats a planned frequency under 2 exposures per household per month as a planning error to fix immediately.
facts.quote: treat anything under 2 as a planning error to fix immediately

facts.fact: Adwave says past roughly 8-10 monthly exposures per household, additional repetition buys little and can irritate.
facts.quote: past roughly 8-10 monthly exposures, additional repetition buys little and can irritate

facts.fact: Adwave's step-by-step planning guidance sets a building-recognition frequency target of 4-6 monthly exposures.
facts.quote: Building recognition: 4-6 monthly. Maintaining it: 2-3. Deadline event: 1-2 across the event window.

facts.fact: Adwave's planning guidance sets a maintenance frequency target of 2-3 monthly exposures.
facts.quote: Maintaining it: 2-3.

facts.fact: Adwave's planning guidance sets a deadline-event frequency target of 1-2 exposures across the event window.
facts.quote: Deadline event: 1-2 across the event window.

facts.fact: In Adwave's dentist scenario, $750/month targeting 8,000 households (3 zips) yields 30,000 impressions, about 3.75x frequency.
facts.quote: | Dentist, new practice | $750/month | 8,000 households (3 zips) | 30,000 impressions ≈ 3.75x frequency |

facts.fact: In Adwave's scenario, $750/month targeting the full metro of 250,000 households yields 30,000 impressions, about 0.12x frequency.
facts.quote: | Same dentist, tempted by metro | $750/month | 250,000 households (full metro) | 30,000 impressions ≈ 0.12x frequency |

facts.fact: In Adwave's furniture store scenario, $5,000/month reaching 150,000 households yields 200,000 impressions, about 1.3x frequency.
facts.quote: | Furniture store, 25 years known | $5,000/month | 150,000 households | 200,000 impressions ≈ 1.3x frequency |

facts.fact: Adwave's pool-service example: 12,000 households at 5x monthly requires 60,000 impressions, or $1,500 at a $25 CPM, which exceeds a $1,000 budget.
facts.quote: That's 60,000 impressions, or $1,500 at a $25 CPM. Their budget is $1,000

facts.fact: Adwave's med spa example states that a business needing 30 new clients a quarter needs about 15,000 of the right households.
facts.quote: A med spa that needs 30 new clients a quarter doesn't need 400,000 households to know it exists; it needs 15,000 of the right households

facts.fact: Adwave's sequencing guidance says a $750/month campaign can grow into a $3,000/month campaign through ring-based expansion.
facts.quote: This is how a $750/month campaign becomes a $3,000/month campaign

facts.fact: Adwave's page is dated June 18, 2026.
Flighting is described as four weeks on and four weeks off.
facts.quote: Flighting** concentrates the same dollars into heavier frequency for shorter windows: four weeks on, four off.

facts.fact: Adwave states that regenerating creative takes about two minutes.
facts.quote: regeneration takes about two minutes on Adwave and fresh creative resets the wear-out clock.

facts.fact: Adwave describes a completion rate of 90% or higher as a sign that creative is wearing well at high frequency.
facts.quote: High frequency with strong completion (90%+) means the creative is wearing well.

facts.fact: Adwave advises shrinking the audience or extending the flight when average monthly frequency falls below 3.
facts.quote: Below 3 monthly: shrink the audience or extend the flight.

facts.fact: Adwave identifies average monthly frequency above 8 to 10 as saturation.
facts.quote: Above 8-10: you've saturated; widen a ring or bank the budget.

facts.fact: Adwave recommends planning 3 to 6 exposures per household per month while building recognition.
facts.quote: Plan for 3-6 exposures per household per month while building recognition, with 3 as the working floor

facts.fact: Adwave states that established brands can maintain on 2 to 3 exposures per household per month.
facts.quote: Established brands can maintain on 2-3.

facts.fact: Adwave advises fixing any TV plan whose monthly frequency lands under 2 per targeted household.
facts.quote: fix any plan that lands under 2.

facts.fact: Adwave suggests rotating two or three creative variations and replacing the weakest variation monthly.
facts.quote: rotate two or three creative variations so the household sees the brand repeatedly but not the identical spot, and replace the weakest variation monthly.

facts.fact: Adwave describes its AI creative generation as free.
facts.quote: With free, two-minute AI generation, creative rotation costs attention rather than money.
